q: The magnetic field is a region where magnetic effects can be ____.
e: A magnetic field is defined as the spatial region around a magnet where its magnetic influence can be detected.

q: The magnetic field is a ____ where magnetic effects can be detected.
e: A magnetic field is defined as the spatial region around a magnet where its magnetic influence can be detected.

q: Distribution of magnetic field can be visualized by the magnetic lines of ____.
e: Magnetic lines of force are used to visually represent the distribution and direction of a magnetic field.

q: Distribution of magnetic field can be ____ by the magnetic lines of force.
e: Magnetic lines of force provide a visual representation of how the magnetic field is distributed in space.

q: The magnetic lines of force leave north pole and ____ south pole.
e: By convention, magnetic lines of force are drawn emerging from the north pole and entering the south pole.

q: The magnetic lines of force leave ____ pole and enter south pole.
e: By convention, magnetic lines of force are drawn emerging from the north pole and entering the south pole.

q: To show the pattern of a magnetic field around a bar magnet, we can sprinkle ____ lightly on a paper, with a bar magnet underneath, and tapping the paper gently.
e: Iron filings align themselves along the magnetic lines of force, revealing the magnetic field pattern when the paper is tapped.

q: To show the pattern of a magnetic field around a bar magnet, we can sprinkle iron filings lightly on a paper, with a bar magnet ____, and tapping the paper gently.
e: Placing the magnet underneath the paper allows the iron filings on top to align with the magnetic field.

q: Figure 10.6 shows the iron filings falling into a certain pattern which is the magnetic ____ pattern.
e: The pattern formed by the iron filings represents the magnetic field pattern of the bar magnet.
The Earth itself acts as a giant magnet, generating its own magnetic field.

q: In other words, we can think of the Earth as having an imaginary bar magnet inside it with magnetic north and south ____ as shown in Figure 10.7.
e: The Earth's magnetic field can be modeled as if there were an imaginary bar magnet with north and south poles inside the planet.

q: The magnetic north lies somewhere in the sea in northern ____ but has been shifting slowly over the years.
e: The Earth's magnetic north pole is currently located in the sea near northern Canada and drifts over time.

q: The magnetic north lies somewhere in the sea in northern Canada but has been shifting slowly over the ____.
e: The Earth's magnetic north pole is not fixed and has been shifting slowly over the years.

q: Magnetic fields can also be found in the interior of atoms and in stars and other ____ bodies.
e: Magnetic fields are a universal phenomenon, existing within atoms, stars, and other celestial bodies.

q: Magnetic fields can also be found in the interior of atoms and in ____ and other celestial bodies.
e: Magnetic fields are a universal phenomenon, existing within atoms, stars, and other celestial bodies.

q: A magnetic field has neither a starting point nor an end point because magnets never have a ____ in contrast to a point electric charge.
e: Unlike electric charges which can exist as isolated monopoles, magnetic poles always exist in pairs, meaning magnetic field lines form continuous loops.
